script.analysis: All 20,200 stored characters read in three contiguous ranges with canonical hash match. Hook: $40K happy Civic owner versus stressed BMW six-figure earner; early subscribe CTA. Core claim: mindset -> behavior -> outcomes cycle; Person A vs Person B at $70K (scarcity vs tool beliefs; B "doubles income" in 10 years). Appeals to an unnamed decades-long study claiming beliefs at 25 predict net worth at 55 "with remarkable accuracy". Sections: money as neutral tool, promotion-avoidance anecdote, problems as puzzles, present bias and delayed gratification, rewiring "neural pathways", noticing reactions and language ("I can't afford" vs "not a priority"), five-people social influence, failure as tuition with a seven-rental-property anecdote, owner versus consumer thinking ($1,000 course ROI), purpose, scarcity versus abundance and self-worth, close. Generic motivational structure with no data visuals implied, no numeric worked examples beyond course ROI, unverified personal anecdotes ("I know someone"), and survivorship framing ("every successful investor"). Present-bias concept is real; most causal claims are unsupported. Heavy ASR noise ("in hair or corently evil pinging", "taught to despy", "Heights.") preserved; not audio-verified.

claim_audit: 0:7000 "Biggest predictor of long-term financial success isn't salary, education or family" contradicts mainstream wealth research where income, education, inheritance and family background are strong wealth predictors; mindset may matter but the comparative superlative is unsupported. Unnamed study "followed thousands over decades", "controlling for education, starting income and family background", predicting age-55 net worth from age-25 beliefs "with remarkable accuracy" - no author, dataset or effect size; not verifiable and should be treated as unsupported. Person B "doubled income" in 10 years is illustrative, not evidence.

7000:14000 Present bias is an established behavioral-economics concept, described reasonably. "You become the average of the five people" is a motivational aphorism, not a research finding. "Rewire neural pathways" is a loose metaphor. Language reframing advice ("not a priority") has no evidence presented. Claim that people "stick with guaranteed poverty" rather than risk failure ignores real downside risk for low-wealth households.

14000:20200 Seven-rental-property anecdote is unverified and survivorship-biased (failed second attempts not shown). $1,000 course framed as investment if it raises income by >$1,000 omits probability of payoff and time cost. "Enough money for everyone" abundance framing is a belief statement, not an economic claim with evidence. No tax, statistic or product claims requiring primary-source checks beyond the unsupported study.

Mechanisms invoked: beliefs shaping behavior, present bias, social influence, risk tolerance, self-worth. Very saturated self-help adjacent topic; this version offers few concrete tools or data and relies on assertions and anecdotes.
